tweets.title: GCAP’s decision to avoid an adaptive-cycle engine in favor of a more conventional architecture is an interesting one. The rationale appears to be reducing technical complexity while still targeting the thrust required for a sixth-generation fighter like Tempest. What’s particularly intriguing is the US has often pursued highly ambitious technologies first, & then circle back to conventional solutions after weighing cost, complexity, and maintainability. This makes a good case study for India as we plan our own future fighter engine roadmap.
